name: Baby tracking
intro: Where the feed and sleep log taps one-handed at 3am and syncs with your partner, and where data goes missing.

apps.title: Mango Baby: Newborn Tracker
apps.verdict: The best iOS tracker in this group: Lock Screen Live Activities, Siri shortcuts, widgets, a one-time payment with no subscription, and generous sharing. The only real limitation is iOS-only, so an Android partner cannot join.
apps.loved: Lock Screen widgets and Live Activities show the current timer without unlocking the phone.
apps.weak: No Android version, so one parent on Android is left out entirely.
apps.whoFor: iOS families looking for a tracker with no monthly subscription

quotes.text: My wife & I love this app to track our baby's activity! The best part is the widgets you can use on the Lock Screen that keep an eye on timers (such as timers for sleep and nursing). The only minor inconvenience is that you have to open the app to update the timers sometimes. For example, if my wife

I love this app for logging! Activities I wish you could manually add other activities but since my baby is a newborn the presets are fine! The other thing that would be great is if it was compatible with android users for other members of my family to log info.

apps.title: Nara Baby & Pregnancy Tracker
apps.verdict: Nara wins on multi-caregiver mode: grandma, dad, and the nanny all work in one shared log in real time. Recent updates broke the timers, which is frustrating, but the core tracking is solid.
apps.loved: Multiple caregivers can see current feeding and sleep status simultaneously without calling each other.
apps.weak: After recent updates, feeding and sleep timers periodically freeze or fail to stop.
apps.whoFor: Families with multiple caregivers who need a live shared log

quotes.text: Look, it's good and helpful but sometimes the timers don't start or stop.. sometimes data just disappears. But when it works it's great

I had started with huckleberry but with multiple caregivers, Nara outperforms wort multiple caregiver logins and does what it's supposed to - track activities. I wasn't looking for any Ai features so Nara has been great.
Two quality of life changes that would make it infinitely better: 1. Add a numpad when entering the time. It's hard to get the exact time when you're scrolling through 60 list items.

apps.title: PiyoLog Baby Feeding Tracker
apps.verdict: A reliable free tracker with real multi-device sync that parents use across two or three kids in a row. The main downside is a 5-minute time step instead of exact timestamps, which annoys meticulous loggers.
apps.loved: Free multi-device sync that the whole family and nanny actually use.
apps.weak: Feeding start time is recorded in 5-minute increments rather than to the second.
apps.whoFor: Large families and parents who bring in grandparents and nannies

quotes.text: Love the app! I used it for over a year now and the free version is sufficient for our needs! You can sync with multiple devices so it is very convenient to share baby status with other care takers and family members! I wish I could give 10 stars! Highly recommended!

App is great especially for allowing multiple people to update the logs. I would like them to add the amount per feed along with the feeding time in a single view in the summary. This allows us to see more easily see a pattern in our baby's daily feed schedule.

apps.title: Baby Tracker: breast feeding +
apps.verdict: A free tracker with a broad set of parameters and good readability of daily data. Partner sync is absent, which is the main limitation for family use.
apps.loved: Quickly log feedings and diapers one-handed at three in the morning.
apps.weak: No shared access for a second parent or nanny.
apps.whoFor: Mothers keeping a solo diary

quotes.text: I do love this app! Even shared it with friends. I wish there was a way my husband/partner could download the app and us use it together on our individual phones. I also wish there was a connection to my Apple Watch because usually my hands are busy and I don't know where my phone is- trying to reme

apps.title: Baby Feed Timer, breastfeeding
apps.verdict: Baby Feed Timer does the main job well: quick logging of breast, bottle, and pump feedings without extra screens. Analytics are minimal, and the shared account with a partner occasionally goes out of sync.
apps.loved: One-tap timer start at three in the morning without having to think.
apps.weak: Sleep analytics do not separate daytime and nighttime sleep, and history is limited to seven days.
apps.whoFor: Breastfeeding mothers who need a fast, accurate log with no extras

quotes.text: The app is fantastic for tracking your baby's needs like feeds, diapers, sleep, meds, etc. I use the widget on my home screen for quick glances so I know when my son is due for a feed or nap. Recently, however, the feed timer in the widget randomly stopped working. I'm not sure why, but I can't get

apps.title: Baby Daybook - Newborn Tracker
apps.verdict: One of the best all-in-one trackers: covers feeding, sleep, diapers, growth, and temperature, has widgets, and supports multiple caregivers. The main issue in recent months is intrusive ad banners in the free version and Lock Screen widgets disappearing after one of the updates.
apps.loved: Lock Screen widgets give instant access to feeding and diaper status without unlocking the phone.
apps.weak: After recent updates, Lock Screen widgets stopped working for many users, removing the app's primary convenience.
apps.whoFor: Couples with multiple caregivers who need a complete log with quick access from any screen

quotes.text: I've been using this app for almost 2.5 years and am using it it for my second child now. I loved the widget feature and then a couple of weeks ago it disappeared! I really like being able to see how long it's been since I've fed or changed my newborn. Please bring back the widget!!

I am on baby number 2 with this app. It has been part of my life daily and since baby number 1. I love every thoughtful feature and is designed perfectly into my lifestyle. I can tell the pedestrian everything they need to know because I've kept track of it all.

apps.title: Pump Log® - Track Breast Milk
apps.verdict: The best dedicated pumping log on the market: timer, daily and weekly volume totals, freezer stock tracking, and reminders all work reliably. The weak spots are occasional crashes that lose a session, plus an inaccurate next-session calculation (it counts from the start of the previous session, not the end).
apps.loved: Visual stats covering the entire feeding journey provide motivation to keep pumping even on hard days.
apps.weak: The next pumping timer counts from the start of the previous session rather than the end, which skews the actual interval.
apps.whoFor: Exclusive pumping mothers who need detailed volume analytics

apps.title: Breastfeeding + Baby Tracker
apps.verdict: One of the strongest free trackers with real multi-device sync that grandmas and rotating-shift dads actually use, and pediatric reports help at appointments. Sync occasionally lags by several hours, and ads in the free version can be inappropriate at times.
apps.loved: Free core features cover feeding, diapers, sleep, and pumping, syncing data for all caregivers.
apps.weak: Sync between devices sometimes falls several hours behind.
apps.whoFor: Couples doing shift care, especially when grandparents are involved

quotes.text: Never question when you gave meds or fed last. Track all your ounces pumped, see how much baby is drinking in real time when you're away. Pediatrician reports that have kept me as an informed parent. I was able to tell the doctor the last antibiotic they took and how many ear infections they have ha

apps.title: Baby Tracker - Newborn Tracker
apps.verdict: Built for a Chinese audience: clean interface, growth curves in place, basic feeding and sleep parameters covered. Sync works for most users, but account registration is blocked outside China, which cuts the audience. Ad lag is annoying.
apps.loved: Clear growth curves and a clean interface that is understandable from the first launch.
apps.weak: Account registration is unavailable outside China, and shared access does not work for some users.
apps.whoFor: Chinese-speaking parents looking for a simple visual tracker

apps.title: Baby Tracker & Newborn Log
apps.verdict: One of the most battle-tested trackers: parents use it across multiple kids for years. Multi-device sync is unreliable, and frequent redesigns break familiar navigation paths.
apps.loved: Covers the full range: feedings, diapers, sleep, growth, and medical events all in one place without extra screens.
apps.weak: Real-time sync between partners regularly falls behind or drops entries.
apps.whoFor: Couples who need a shared log for two with a history spanning years

quotes.text: This app was a lifesaver for our first child. Just to be able to look at the app and know why he was crying because he's he hungry or tired. Now with my second kid I really utilize the widget to see when last ate on my Home Screen. It truly save me so I don't have to remember the last time I did something

Been using this app for nearly two years now and the performance is heading in the wrong direction. My wife and I both use the app and often times data entered by one person doesn't appear for the other until we force quit the app and reopen

Good app - like the ability to see the data graphically, but some UI issues. Wish there was a dark mode option so I don't have to stare at a bright screen at night time. Also wish I could toggle between feeds, pumping, diaper changes, etc.

apps.title: Baby Connect: Baby Tracker
apps.verdict: One of the most full-featured trackers with a long history: feeding, diapers, temperature, vaccines, and multi-user access. The downside is that entries occasionally disappear and message notifications do not reach some users.
apps.loved: Daily summaries and feeding statistics that can be shown to a pediatrician right from the phone.
apps.weak: Sync across multiple caregivers is unreliable: messages do not arrive, and there is no permission separation between a parent and a nanny.
apps.whoFor: Families with multiple caregivers and monthly pediatric visits

quotes.text: I love the idea of this app, but it's been really frustrating to use because it randomly deletes past breastfeeding entries and data. I log every feeding, including how long my baby feeds on each breast, and I rely on that information to track patterns and review the data summaries.

With my daughter she would get constipated and doctors asked me to track her bowel movements, this app made it easy to coordinate with the nanny as well as our family when it came to diaper changes. We are also able to keep track of meds and times. Vaccinations etc .. is a great app

Would be a lot better if there was an administrator/teacher view vs parent. It allows anyone to edit whatever has been entered for sleep or meals instead of it just showing as an update on the parents end.

apps.title: Huckleberry: Baby & Child
apps.verdict: The best functional newborn log in this group: predicts the optimal nap window, keeps a detailed feeding and sleep journal, and works across two devices. The main product flaw is that widgets and voice input are locked behind a paywall.
apps.loved: The "sweet spot" window predictor genuinely helps catch the right moment before the baby gets overtired.
apps.weak: The home screen widget requires a subscription, even though a quick glance at the last feeding time is the main value at three in the morning.
apps.whoFor: Parents of a newborn who are willing to pay for a smart sleep predictor

quotes.text: It would be the perfect app if it allowed lock screen to also show other tasks we want to monitor how it does for last feeding. I would like my lock screen to show last diaper change and last pump so I can quickly see if I'm due. Would make stress management much easier with a quick look rather than

I always accidentally hit the save button when I'm in the middle of nursing. It doesn't give you the option to edit and continue the timer. But it allows you to change the minutes. Wish it let you just resume the timer. Annoying feature.
Helping to identify the sleepy cues by knowing the predicted naps has been a life saver!!! I have recommended this app to all new moms I know of!! It is absolutely worth the subscription!

The last thing a tired mom wants to do is think more…the scroll clock (which is already annoying) doesn't automatically switch to AM or PM when you scroll like it does in your calendar etc. But why not make it easy to type in the time? It's the one huge flaw with this app imo.

Update your app. When I roll the time back from 12:01AM to 11:55PM to put a feeding in accurately, why does the date not automatically change. If I'm trying to enter a future date, maybe change the date for me? As a new parent this is infuriating. Poor development.

apps.title: Erby feeding & sleep tracker
apps.verdict: A clean interface, customizable widgets, and a wide set of parameters make Erby comfortable for everyday use. Cases of complete data loss during sync errors undermine trust, but overall users praise stable operation.
apps.loved: Customizable home screen widgets reduce the number of taps to a minimum.
apps.weak: A sync error can wipe data from both devices at once.
apps.whoFor: Parents who value a tidy design and widgets

quotes.text: App was not syncing with Android although account is premium. Once I deleted the app from Android, all data got deleted in iOS as well. Everything is gone. All records. Do not trust

apps.title: BabyTime (Record & Analysis)
apps.verdict: The app handles basic logging well and offers shared access, but one update broke sync, which is critical for families who had relied on it for years. The Apple Watch widget exists but is unreliable.
apps.loved: Real shared access in real time, when everything is working.
apps.weak: Timer sync between partners does not work reliably.
apps.whoFor: Couples who track together

quotes.text: I love this app, my husband and I use it to track Baby's activities. I especially love that functionality on the Apple Watch was added, makes quick entries a snap. I've given the app 4 stars because the widget is unreliable. Sometimes it works but often it won't update.

apps.title: Ovia Parenting & Baby Tracker
apps.verdict: Ovia's strength is its ecosystem: users move from a cycle tracker to a pregnancy app to a baby tracker without losing context. Feeding, sleep, and diapers are simple to log, but there is no dark mode, multi-caregiver access is hard to set up, and the last-used breast side occasionally resets.
apps.loved: A continuous ecosystem from family planning through infancy, plus a rich article library with age-targeted advice.
apps.weak: No dark mode, and the editorial feed surfaces irrelevant tips ahead of schedule, cluttering the screen at three in the morning.
apps.whoFor: Mothers who already used Ovia during pregnancy

quotes.text: The app is exactly what you'd need if you want to keep track of diapers and feeds. It does have helpful tips and milestone markers. My main complaint though it doesn't have a dark mode. Turning this app on at 4am for a feed is the worst, even with brightness all the way down.
Customer service is non existent. I would have given 5 stars as I love the ap but can't invite my husband and nanny in the ap

apps.title: Baby Tracker Pro (Newborn Log)
apps.verdict: A stable tracker with Apple Watch support and a long reputation among parents on their second or third child, but partner sync breaks, Siri Shortcuts are partially implemented, and the Pro version adds less than it promises.
apps.loved: Apple Watch support and pediatric reports that genuinely impress the doctor at an appointment.
apps.weak: Shared access for two parents requires a separate purchase for each, and sync periodically breaks.
apps.whoFor: Tech-savvy parents with an iPhone and Apple Watch

quotes.text: I can't set a nursing timer and go back to the list of other options. Timer is cancelled automatically if I want to check when my baby woke up etc. Apple Watch wouldn't even start timers. I tap nursing->right, and it says "transfer timed out". I want my

This app is great for tracking everything Baby and the pediatrician is always so impressed how much data we have. I just wish it had an option to track a bottle that is part expressed milk and part formula so it didn't show as 2 feedings.

apps.title: Cubtale: Pregnancy & Baby
apps.verdict: Cubtale offers smart NFC milk tags, a timer from the watch, and flexible per-caregiver customization. But data disappears without warning, the sleep timer resets on its own, and the Watch app stops working after a few days with no notice.
apps.loved: A feeding timer right from the Apple Watch and a last-side reminder in total darkness without picking up the phone.
apps.weak: Entries disappear without explanation, and in the paid version ads are placed right next to journal buttons, which is especially disruptive at night.
apps.whoFor: Families with nannies and distributed care who need a shared log

quotes.text: Since the most recent update, we are unable to use the sleep tracking feature across multiple devices with the same login. Only the device that started the timer can close it but the history shows up on all devices. This is very frustrating because multiple timers can be going at the same time for t

I am a nanny for 3 small children including an infant under 1 and I am loving this app so far! Love that I can start a timer or record an event from my apple watch! I would really like to see the added feature of being able to add a photo/video to any event log

apps.title: Onoco: Baby Tracker & Schedule
apps.verdict: A beautifully designed tracker with shared access and sleep predictions, but feeding timers regularly freeze or reset and sync between partners is uneven. High potential, stability lets it down.
apps.loved: Shared access for both parents with predictions for the next feeding.
apps.weak: The feeding timer freezes and switches sides on its own, especially at night.
apps.whoFor: Couples who share night duty

quotes.text: The nap time predictions are more accurate than I am just watching her cues half the time only issue is they seem to not think my lo should be awake between 8-10 and won't give predictions if she is so we just go off cues

apps.title: Napper: Baby Sleep Tracker
apps.verdict: Napper does its main job well: it predicts the next nap based on past ones and clearly shows total sleep time for the day. Multi-caregiver sync is present. But feeding and diaper logging are secondary, predictions sometimes fail to adjust for the baby's age, and the interface became more confusing after the latest update.
apps.loved: Next sleep window prediction based on actual previous sleep time helps plan the day and prevent overtiredness.
apps.weak: The algorithm often ignores the baby's age, continuing to recommend 4 naps a day for a baby who has long outgrown that schedule.
apps.whoFor: Parents who need an accurate sleep tracker with predictions rather than a general-purpose journal

quotes.text: I used to try to keep notes of her naps and would forget. This app makes it easy with reminders of when naps should occur. It accurately predicts nap time and length, bedtime and morning wakes! All super helpful when planning my day and preventing overtired bebe :)

apps.title: Baby + | Your Baby Tracker
apps.verdict: Baby+ by Philips has a clean interface and good coverage: feeding, sleep, diapers, medication, and growth. The weak spot is no dark mode, which is critical for nighttime use, and data occasionally disappears after the app is closed.
apps.loved: Medication tracker with reminders and WHO growth percentile comparisons all in one place.
apps.weak: No dark mode, and the bright white screen at minimum brightness at three in the morning irritates even the most loyal users.
apps.whoFor: Solo parents for whom reliable medication and growth logging matters

quotes.text: The fact that there is no nighttime setting is extremely off putting. App is way too use and helps me keep track of all my baby's data. I especially use it to track feeding, but the stark whiteness of the app is so jarring during middle of the night, even with my brightness all the way down, it's t

apps.title: Baby Tracker!
apps.verdict: An all-in-one tracker covering feedings, sleep, diapers, growth, and medications. The main pain point is no real-time device sync, so both parents cannot log simultaneously, plus an awkward time-entry dial that developers keep removing and bringing back.
apps.loved: Broad category coverage in one app gives a complete picture of the day without switching between multiple journals.
apps.weak: No real-time sync between devices, so two parents cannot keep the log simultaneously.
apps.whoFor: Families with one primary caregiver who needs a complete offline log

quotes.text: Love the simplicity of this app, however it assumes there's is only one caregiver so there is no way to share data in real time. You have to manually export and email the data to another caregiver. There is no account that all the info gets uploaded to, which would be useful if multiple caregivers l

When I first got this app it had the annoying clock that you had to physically move when adding in times for feeding or naps.... then they updated it to an easier to use system so I could easily select the hour and minute. After the most recent update, it went back to the clock. It's so frustrating

apps.title: Baby Tracker・Breastfeeding Log
apps.verdict: The app covers the full basic set and works across platforms, but after the latest update the sleep timer disappears when the app is closed, and sync between partners lags at critical nighttime moments.
apps.loved: Cross-platform: one log works on iPhone, iPad, and Android at the same time.
apps.weak: After the update, the sleep timer stops when the app is backgrounded and data is lost.
apps.whoFor: Mixed iOS-Android families with multiple caregivers

quotes.text: Great app - we use it on iPhone, iPad & android devices. Has more functionality under Statistics for Android than for Apple devices but is better than some of the other apps we've tried.

apps.title: Happy Baby - Sleep & Tracker
apps.verdict: The app focuses on sleep prediction and scheduling, but the algorithm is inconsistent and sometimes gives recommendations that contradict the baby's actual routine. Basic feeding and diaper tracking is present but shallow.
apps.loved: Live Lock Screen widgets for quick logging of sleep start and end.
apps.weak: The schedule prediction algorithm does not learn accurately enough from the baby's real data.
apps.whoFor: Parents who want to build a sleep schedule by the clock

apps.title: Baby Tracker - Newborn Log
apps.verdict: A simple free newborn log with a home screen widget. It does the basic job well enough, but a recent update moved buttons to the top and cleared the bottom for ads, significantly hurting one-handed usability at night.
apps.loved: The home screen widget lets you check the last feeding time without opening the app.
apps.weak: After the redesign, buttons ended up at the top of the screen, making one-handed use at three in the morning awkward.
apps.whoFor: Parents who need a free basic log with no extras

quotes.text: This app was a lifesaver for our first child. Just to be able to look at the app and know why he was crying because he's he hungry or tired. Now with my second kid I really utilize the widget to see when last ate on my Home Screen. It truly save me so I don't have to remember the last time I did something

Been using this app for nearly two years now and the performance is heading in the wrong direction. My wife and I both use the app and often times data entered by one person doesn't appear for the other until we force quit the app and reopen

Good app - like the ability to see the data graphically, but some UI issues. Wish there was a dark mode option so I don't have to stare at a bright screen at night time. Also wish I could toggle between feeds, pumping, diaper changes, etc.

apps.title: Cloud Baby Monitor
apps.verdict: Cloud Baby Monitor smartly turns a spare phone or tablet into a baby monitor without buying dedicated hardware. Connection quality is unstable, there is no night vision, and video lag is noticeable.
apps.loved: Turn an old iPad into a full baby monitor for free without additional hardware.
apps.weak: Video regularly freezes or drops connection, sometimes showing a sleeping baby who has already woken up.
apps.whoFor: Anyone with a spare Apple device who does not want to buy a separate monitor

apps.title: Feed Baby - Breastfeeding App
apps.verdict: Free Apple Watch support sets this app apart from competitors, and logging for a solo user is convenient. But sync between phones is chaotic enough that a couple cannot rely on it, and data can disappear completely.
apps.loved: Full Apple Watch control in one hand while the other holds the baby.
apps.weak: Sync between devices is locked for 6 hours in the free version and still periodically fails, making shared tracking unreliable.
apps.whoFor: Breastfeeding mothers logging solo with an Apple Watch

quotes.text: My wife and I both purchased the app and it will not sync our baby on our phones. We have emailed support and reached out on their only support service through Facebook and they will not respond. If you have a baby and are needing a tracking app DO NOT get this one. There is no support.

This was a very helpful app to use in the first month of my child's life, when all of a sudden all of the logged information along with her entire profile disappeared in the middle of tracking a feed. There seems to be no way to retrieve all of the lost information.

This is the only way I keep track of feeding. This morning I woke up in a startle after a long hard night with baby and I thought I had missed a feed. Thanks to logging on the app I managed to piece together what happened last night and figure out that I hadn't missed any feed.

apps.title: Talli Baby Tracker Newborn Log
apps.verdict: A unique concept with physical buttons at the changing table solves the main tracking-without-a-phone problem, and sync across multiple caregivers works. But frequent auth failures and service outages make the log unreliable exactly when it is needed most.
apps.loved: A physical device with buttons at the changing table lets you log feeding and sleep one-handed without touching the phone.
apps.weak: The server goes down for several days at a time, and auth errors lock users out of their data at the worst possible moment.
apps.whoFor: Couples with a shared changing-table station who are willing to buy a physical device

quotes.text: I really like this app, but my husband can't use it because they haven't updated the version in the Samsung store! Please fix ASAP!!

apps.title: Baby's Journal
apps.verdict: A simple free tracker with convenient feeding and diaper logging. Multi-account device sync, reminders, and a medication section are all missing.
apps.loved: Minimalist interface: logging a feeding takes seconds even at three in the morning.
apps.weak: No real multi-caregiver sync: a partner on a different iCloud account sees a blank screen.
apps.whoFor: Solo parents who need a free basic journal with nothing extra

apps.title: Glow Baby Tracker & Growth App
apps.verdict: Glow Baby covers all tracking categories and works, but constant pop-up ads for breast pumps ruin the experience even for paying subscribers. Sync between users is unreliable.
apps.loved: Everything in one place: feeding, diapers, sleep, and growth, with convenient widgets.
apps.weak: Ads for a branded pump pop up in the middle of logging a diaper at four in the morning and cannot be disabled.
apps.whoFor: Anyone willing to tolerate aggressive cross-promotion in exchange for broad functionality

apps.title: Baby Feeding Log
apps.verdict: A minimalist feeding and diaper tracker with no clutter: quick to launch, quick to log. But there is no sync between parents' phones, no next-feeding reminders, no manual duration entry, and the timer sometimes stops in the background. Fine for one caregiver, not for two.
apps.loved: Maximum interface simplicity lets you log a feeding one-handed in the dark in two seconds.
apps.weak: No device sync, no next-feeding reminders, and no manual duration entry for missed entries.
apps.whoFor: Solo mothers or families with one primary feeder who need only a feeding log

quotes.text: Used this app for a few weeks. I'd start the timer, not close the app but use others with this in the background. About half the time I'd come back to the app and it would open without the timer running, like it was being opened for the first time. Super frustrating.

apps.title: Pregnancy + | Tracker App
apps.verdict: A well-designed pregnancy tracker with 3D animation, multiple baby-size comparison formats, and weekly videos. The focus is on pregnancy, not the newborn period.
apps.loved: Multiple baby-size comparison formats (fruit, animals, desserts) and beautiful 3D models make weekly updates feel like an event.
apps.weak: The contraction counter, previously free, is now behind a subscription.
apps.whoFor: Pregnant women who want an aesthetic weekly development diary

apps.title: The Wonder Weeks - Baby leaps
apps.verdict: An app for predicting developmental leaps based on the Wonder Weeks book. It gives context for a baby's fussy behavior, but accuracy varies and depends on the individual child.
apps.loved: Parents whose babies match the model feel relief: they understand the reason for fussiness in advance.
apps.weak: The leap window is vague (plus or minus a week or two), and when it does not match the baby, it feels like money wasted.
apps.whoFor: Parents who want to explain fussy behavior through a developmental leap model

quotes.text: I have used this app for all 4 of my children now and I swear by the accuracy of the leaps! I love the suggested activities to enhance each leap and the skills baby is learning! Knowing potential reasons behind the "storms" is very helpful, especially to prepare a bit in advance for them!
I used this for my first born in 2020/2021 and it was so helpful. It helped me understand my baby's brain, their needs, and it helped me understand that I wasn't messing up when he'd become fussier.

I feel like it's a little behind on actual development. My baby was born early so I feel like her jumps are more aligned with her actual birth date vs her estimated delivery date which was what the app recommended

Update: adding some stars after experiencing great customer service support to address my issues with the app. Major regrets in purchasing this. Several parents recommended it and in a fog of new parent delirium I paid for a subscription. It "predicts" fussy episodes BUT with a 1-2 week window

We've used the wonder weeks app with all three of our kiddos. It helps give context to what our infants are going through, how we can help them, and milestones we can look out for. Nothing in this app says these milestones HAVE to happen but that they could be happening. We use the app to track fuss

apps.title: Nanit
apps.verdict: Nanit is primarily a camera monitor, and sleep tracking is a bonus. Auto-detection of lay-down and wake-up frequently makes mistakes, and audio leaking in the background is annoying.
apps.loved: Peace of mind for a new parent: video stream, breathing band, and weekly sleep summaries all in one place.
apps.weak: Automatic sleep tracking regularly confuses a brief waking with a full wake-up, and manual corrections change nothing.
apps.whoFor: Anyone who already bought a Nanit camera and wants sleep insights alongside it

apps.title: Hatch Grow
apps.verdict: When it works, logging is convenient: feeding, sleep, and diapers on one screen. But the app crashes so regularly that many users describe a daily ritual of deleting and reinstalling it, and one user lost 17 months of data.
apps.loved: Deep integration with Hatch smart scales and the changing pad for automatic weight recording.
apps.weak: No way to edit or delete entries, and self-starting timers plus data loss when switching phones undermine trust in the log.
apps.whoFor: Hatch hardware owners who are willing to tolerate instability for the sake of the ecosystem

quotes.text: I have been using this app for 17 months. It was working great until about 2 weeks ago. Random timers would start unprompted, entries would be added on its own, entries would disappear. Now my child has disappeared and all my logs are gone. I can't even log in.

apps.title: BabyPage: Baby Book & Journal
apps.verdict: BabyPage is a digital photo album with prompts and ready-made templates, not a feeding and sleep journal. It works well for milestones and printing a book, but it is not a newborn tracker at all. Frequent crashes with loss of unsaved pages are a serious problem.
apps.loved: Ready-made prompts for every stage of the first year let you create a beautiful keepsake book with no design skills.
apps.weak: The app crashes while editing pages and loses unsaved changes, making book creation unpredictable.
apps.whoFor: Parents who want to create a printed photo album of the first year

apps.title: Lansinoh Smartpump 2.0 App
apps.verdict: A tracker specifically for breastfeeding mothers with Bluetooth integration for the Lansinoh pump: when the connection is stable, session logging is nearly automatic. But Bluetooth drops, data is lost, and there is no dark mode.
apps.loved: Automatic session recording via Bluetooth with no manual entry.
apps.weak: Bluetooth connection to the pump drops regularly and data is lost without warning.
apps.whoFor: Mothers using a Lansinoh Smartpump 2.0

quotes.text: I use this app to track my premie baby's feeds. It's been okay but there's been a few days when I can't make any entries and that's very frustrating. My daughter is under the 1st percentile for her weight and has been failing to grow. I need to be able to reliably track her feeding for her specialis

apps.title: BabyCenter Pregnancy Tracker
apps.verdict: One of the best informational pregnancy trackers, with an active community and weekly content. The switch to newborn mode happens automatically with no way to revert, which causes problems with overdue pregnancies.
apps.loved: A loyal audience returns for every subsequent pregnancy.
apps.weak: The app forcibly switches to newborn mode at exactly 40 weeks, ignoring the actual due date.
apps.whoFor: First-time mothers during pregnancy, not for newborn logging

apps.title: Momcozy
apps.verdict: This is an ecosystem app for Momcozy breast pumps and monitors, not a general tracker: pumping logging works, but the camera regularly goes offline, notifications are unreliable, and the interface is glitchy. Sleep and diaper tracking are not available.
apps.loved: Convenient logging of pumped volume with scheduled reminders.
apps.weak: Works only with Momcozy devices; no sleep or diaper tracking.
apps.whoFor: Owners of a Momcozy breast pump or monitor

apps.title: Babylist Baby Registry
apps.verdict: A wish-list aggregator for preparing for a baby's arrival: lets you add items from any store into one registry. Gift cards only work in Babylist's own expensive shop, which disappoints gift-givers.
apps.loved: Lets you combine wishes from Amazon, Target, and any other store in one place.
apps.weak: Babylist gift cards can only be spent in the brand's own store, which has a limited selection at premium prices.
apps.whoFor: Anyone putting together a gift list before a baby arrives

apps.title: The Bump: Baby & Pregnancy App
apps.verdict: An informational pregnancy tracker with weekly updates, 3D models, and a community. The built-in feeding timer is buggy: it counts time for both breasts simultaneously and resets when switching sides. The app frequently crashes and logs users out.
apps.loved: Weekly size comparisons and daily development facts make pregnancy easier to follow.
apps.weak: The breastfeeding timer starts on both sides at once, making the nighttime log unreliable.
apps.whoFor: Pregnant women who want weekly updates and a community

apps.title: Smart Sleep Coach by Pampers™
apps.verdict: The app focuses on schedule-based sleep training rather than comprehensive journaling: no proper dark mode, no feeding and diaper screen in one place, and predictions often ignore the baby's individual rhythm. It only works with babies from 12 weeks old, making it useless during the hardest newborn period.
apps.loved: Automatically recalculates the day's schedule after each actual sleep, giving a reference point for the next few hours.
apps.weak: Does not adapt to the individual baby's rhythm: the same advice for everyone, and recommended wake windows often do not match the real baby.
apps.whoFor: Parents ready for strict CIO-method sleep training

quotes.text: For a paid service, the app is lacking in basic features. Basic things I would expect it to have: -Dark mode (hello this app is geared towards sleep and often used at night) -home screen widgets for convenience -Ability to set a bedtime and number of naps without contacting Support
Somehow this predicted my baby's sleep with precision from day one mind blown. Working now to help her sleep better at night.

App has tons of potential and I wanted to like it. The biggest issue I have is that it's not offering appropriate awake time for my baby's age. 2hr wake window with 30-40min naps for 3 month old? I don't think so. I wish I could set targets for wake windows, naps and not only either wake or bed ti

I love this app - my baby is finally getting on a schedule I can work around. There's just one major design flaw, coming from two systems consultants. If we forget to start the sleep at the exact time she goes down, it is really hard to document it properly. There is no way to easily add an ongoing s

apps.title: Breastfeeding Newborn tracker
apps.verdict: A very simple feeding tracker with no account and no cloud: convenient as long as the phone is nearby, but all data is lost when the app is deleted. Internal ads sometimes serve explicit content. Reliability is essentially zero.
apps.loved: Extremely simple breastfeeding timer start with no extra steps.
apps.weak: No account and no cloud storage: all data disappears on reinstall.
apps.whoFor: Mothers who need only a feeding timer with nothing else

quotes.text: Love the simplicity of this app. Does just what I want it to. However, if you navigate away from it while it's timing a feeding, your session is lost. So unless you happened to note the time you began, it's really quite pointless.

apps.title: Pump with Elvie
apps.verdict: Mothers love the Elvie pump itself, but the app is weak: it spontaneously changes recorded milk volume after saving, frequently loses connection to the pump, and crashes. At a pump price of $550, this is a real letdown.
apps.loved: Remote suction level control from the phone screen without lifting a shirt.
apps.weak: The app changes the recorded milk volume on its own, and session data is lost when connection drops.
apps.whoFor: Elvie pump owners who have accepted the app's instability

quotes.text: Please make a dark mode for those who pump in the middle of the night and don't want to be blinded by a bright white screen. Additionally I wish the timer feature would alert you when the time is up while you're using other apps.

apps.title: Baby Breastfeeding Tracker
apps.verdict: The app earned loyalty over years across three or four children, but after the Sunflowr redesign it inserted video ads on launch that play out loud during silent nighttime feedings. Data sync between devices is unstable, and lost entries for mothers of premature babies is a critical problem.
apps.loved: Simple feeding timer with a side marker, proven over ten years.
apps.weak: Video ads play every time the app is opened, including at night during a feeding.
apps.whoFor: Parents who remember the old version and have not yet found a replacement

quotes.text: I paid for the premium version of this app and Im really upset at this point. This is now the 5th time in only 3 weeks that the app didn't save my data. It saves then somehow deletes sometimes a full day of data or even previous days and I NEED this information since I had a preemie.

I've been using this app on and off over the past 10 years with 3 kids. I mainly use the breastfeeding timer to help me remember which side baby last fed and to see changes in trends of her eating. This app needs to support an app on Apple Watch. There's so many times my phone is out of reach especi

apps.title: Motorola Nursery
apps.verdict: Motorola Nursery is a companion for the video monitor, not a standalone feeding and sleep tracker. Video freezes on launch for a significant share of users, and there are no tracking features such as a feeding or diaper journal.
apps.loved: Remote camera viewing outside the home via the mobile app when the connection is stable.
apps.weak: The video stream regularly fails to load on open, which defeats the main purpose of the monitor.
apps.whoFor: Motorola camera owners who need only video access

apps.title: Pregnancy Baby Tracker - WTE
apps.verdict: An informational app for pregnant women with a community and weekly updates. The built-in feeding timer is unstable and unsuitable as a reliable newborn log.
apps.loved: Detailed weekly updates on fetal development reassure first-time parents.
apps.weak: The breastfeeding timer regularly resets and loses data when the app is reopened.
apps.whoFor: Pregnant women, not parents of a newborn

quotes.text: Overall, the app isn't bad, but every time I use it to track my breast-feeding, if I have to reopen the app for any reason it had completely closed out and I have to manually enter my data. It's extremely frustrating that it'll just close out randomly. I'll be switching to another app for tracking f

apps.title: Pregnancy Tracker 3D by Sprout
apps.verdict: Sprout is essentially a pregnancy tracker with 3D visualization, not a newborn tracker. For feeding and sleep logging tasks, parents move to other tools.
apps.loved: Weekly 3D fetal models give a vivid sense of the baby's growth.
apps.weak: No newborn tracking functionality at all: no feedings, no diapers, no sleep.
apps.whoFor: Expectant parents interested in fetal development visualization during pregnancy

apps.title: Baby Milestone Tracker Sprouty
apps.verdict: Sprouty positions itself as a developmental milestone tracker with exercises, but basic feeding and sleep logging is hidden behind a subscription, and the content contains factual errors such as claiming a baby starts walking at 7 weeks. Not suitable for nighttime tracking at three in the morning.
apps.loved: Weekly development exercises and stage descriptions that ease anxiety for new parents.
apps.weak: Factual errors in developmental stage descriptions undermine trust in the medical content.
apps.whoFor: Parents who care more about a development diary than operational tracking

quotes.text: My biggest irritation is that I paid for this app but I have to pay extra to invite my husband to join us. We have 1 child and live in the same household. Why should I have to pay extra for him? Wild.

apps.title: HiMommy: Ovulation & Pregnancy
apps.verdict: This is a pregnancy and early parenthood app, not a feeding and sleep tracker: no time-based feeding log, no sleep charts, no diaper reminders. Trying to use it as a newborn journal will fail on the very first night shift.
apps.loved: Daily fetal development updates by pregnancy week with cell-level detail, appreciated during the waiting period.
apps.weak: Feeding, sleep, and diaper logging are completely absent, meaning the basic functions of a newborn tracker are not implemented.
apps.whoFor: Pregnant women who want to track fetal development week by week

apps.title: Flo Cycle & Period Tracker
apps.verdict: A menstrual cycle and pregnancy tracker, not a newborn diary. It has nothing to do with feedings and diapers.
apps.loved: After ten years, it accurately predicts cycles and ovulation.
apps.weak: All content and features, including basic symptom explanations, are locked behind a subscription.
apps.whoFor: Those planning a pregnancy, not parents of a newborn

apps.title: amma: Pregnancy & Baby Tracker
apps.verdict: Amma positions itself as a pregnancy and new-parent community, but ads and subscription pop-ups on literally every tap make logging at three in the morning unbearable. The feeding and sleep tracker functionality is present but drowns in monetization.
apps.loved: Clear weekly development summaries covering changes in the body and nutrition.
apps.weak: Ads and pop-ups cover tracker buttons on every tap, turning the nighttime log into an obstacle course.
apps.whoFor: Users who value pregnancy content and can tolerate ads

apps.title: Baby Tracker.
apps.verdict: The app attracts with a clean interface, but it regularly loses feeding and sleep data, and the timer glitches mid-feeding. Shared access for two parents is entirely absent, making it useless for couples.
apps.loved: Clean and minimal interface, comfortable for one-handed logging.
apps.weak: No device sync between two parents during night shifts.
apps.whoFor: A solo parent willing to accept lost entries

quotes.text: Love the simplicity of this app, however it assumes there's is only one caregiver so there is no way to share data in real time. You have to manually export and email the data to another caregiver. There is no account that all the info gets uploaded to, which would be useful if multiple caregivers l

When I first got this app it had the annoying clock that you had to physically move when adding in times for feeding or naps.... then they updated it to an easier to use system so I could easily select the hour and minute. After the most recent update, it went back to the clock. It's so frustrating

apps.title: BabyFeed- Baby Feeding Tracker
apps.verdict: A simple interface is appealing, but sync between devices is so unreliable that couples have fed the baby twice due to unsynced entries. Charts crash the app and data disappears. Essentially unworkable as a family tracker.
apps.loved: Minimal screen with no extra buttons, working from the very first second.
apps.weak: Sync between partners fails so often that entries become unreliable.
apps.whoFor: Parents who need the most minimalist single-device tracker

quotes.text: Crashes all the time and I share the data with my partner and we both input but it does not update properly on many occasions. We even ended up double feeding in the night as we had not seen the others input. It simply did not show even though logged in on same account.

apps.title: Medela Family - Breast Feeding
apps.verdict: The idea of Bluetooth sync with a Medela pump is good, but the app's execution does not hold up: constant crashes, unexpected logouts, and lost entries turn a useful tool into a source of stress. Reliability is unacceptably low for a newborn tracker.
apps.loved: Automatic Medela pump stop via the app at 29:59, removing the need to watch the timer during a nighttime pumping session.
apps.weak: The app regularly logs the user out and loses all entries for the day, with no way to recover them.
apps.whoFor: Medela Bluetooth pump owners, provided they accept the instability

apps.title: Pampers Rewards
apps.verdict: A Pampers loyalty app for collecting points on diaper purchases. It has nothing to do with keeping a newborn diary.
apps.loved: Points can be exchanged for coupons and free diapers.
apps.weak: The QR code scanner often fails to focus, and after updates the login breaks for long stretches.
apps.whoFor: Pampers diaper shoppers, not baby care trackers

apps.title: WeMoms - Pregnancy & Baby App
apps.verdict: WeMoms positions itself as a community for pregnant women and new mothers, but ads are so aggressive that reaching the content is nearly impossible. Newborn tracking is secondary here.
apps.loved: A lively community of mothers where it is easy to find support and feel less alone.
apps.weak: The volume of ads literally blocks navigation through the app.
apps.whoFor: Those looking for community support rather than strict tracking

apps.title: Enfamil: Baby Rewards Tracker®
apps.verdict: The Enfamil Tracker is primarily a loyalty program with basic feeding logging as an add-on. Auth breaks regularly, points fail to appear for weeks, and there is no way to edit entries. Not suitable as a newborn tracker.
apps.loved: Feeding and pump tracker in one place with a formula discount program for those already buying it.
apps.weak: The app's core function, rewards tracking, only works through a web browser, and the tracker itself cannot edit entries.
apps.whoFor: Parents buying Enfamil who want to accumulate points with minimal effort

apps.title: Preggers | Pregnancy tracker
apps.verdict: This is a pregnancy tracking app, not a newborn tracker: no feeding, sleep, or diaper logging, and no two-parent sync. It is not relevant for the baby-tracking category.
apps.loved: Clear visualization of fetal growth by week with fruit comparisons.
apps.weak: Not designed for logging newborn feedings, sleep, or diapers.
apps.whoFor: Expectant mothers during pregnancy, not parents of a newborn

apps.title: Pregnancy Tracker・App by Moms
apps.verdict: Pregnancy Tracker by Moms covers the basics for pregnant women, but there is almost no free tier, and newborn tracking is not available at all.
apps.loved: A 3D baby widget on the home screen updates the fetal size each week.
apps.weak: Without a subscription the app shows almost nothing, and basic pregnancy tracking features are behind a paywall.
apps.whoFor: Anyone who wants a visual pregnancy diary and does not mind paying for it

apps.title: Pregnancy Tracker: Baby Bump
apps.verdict: This is a pregnancy tracking app, not a baby tracker. The main problem is a systematic one-week error in due date calculation that developers have not fixed for years. Not suitable for families with a newborn.
apps.loved: Simple and lightweight due date entry with no extra screens.
apps.weak: Due date calculation consistently shows a week ahead, unfixed for several years according to reviews.
apps.whoFor: Pregnant women in early pregnancy who need a minimal app with no baby tracker features

apps.title: TimeHut - Baby Album
apps.verdict: TimeHut is a family photo album, not a newborn feeding and sleep tracker: no timers, no diaper journal, no reminders. It is not relevant for the baby-tracking category, and uploaded photo and video loss makes it unreliable even in its own niche.
apps.loved: A private family album where grandparents can see photos without social media.
apps.weak: Uploaded photos and videos periodically disappear with no way to recover them.
apps.whoFor: Families spread across different cities who want to share photos
